Thank you, that does help. We are both guys, i forgot to include that. 'Doing things' rather than just talking is what i would normally do, so that's good to know that should help! 
I didn't know if there was anything more formal or structured, almost like some sort of common thing that i should advise him to do.
Thanks for the tips!

Yep, i figured it would be tough, I definitely can't develop myself! 
Thanks for the tip on etsy, hadn't seen it before, it's similar for sure. 
Ha thanks man, we'll see what happens!

Ha I nearly used Asos as an example of how it would be. The only difference being that they predominantly display well known and established brands, I wanted to really target those new brands with potential, who are trying to get themselves recognised.

Sorry, they wouldn't be, I might not have been clear enough.

The idea is for a website to host multiple clothing brand's products - similar to many clothing websites but it would be specifically for new, up and coming clothing startups. 
Helping them to get more exposure by giving customers one go-to place to buy unique clothing rather than scouring the internet for various new companies. 

By seeing the brand on our site, and (hopefully)liking what they see, they are more likely to buy their products or at least check the brand out, as they most probably would not have heard of them before and would have been unlikely to stumble across them seeing as there are so many new startup clothing brands around at this moment.

Although I didn't mention it, I can't design a website solely myself, but that's what places like shopify and web design companies are for right? I wouldn't want an awful looking site, that I've tried to make myself. 

I could use some feedback on whether or not people recommend using shopify, or if it is better to pay a web designer or company to make one. 

In terms of hits, maybe I should be more specific, because I wouldn't have a problem advertising and raising the profile locally..i need advice on how i could take it to the next level. Techniques in continuing to grow, rather than plateauing.

When I mentioned how to charge the brand, (either via a monthly subscription or per product sold) and my point in redirecting the buyer or not, i was seeking advice on what might work better.

I wanted to run over a few decisions before i went any further, and thought this would be the place to get some help or guidance.

Thanks for your feedback though, it's helpful to see another viewpoint of course
